mappings.note: Matches latitude, altitude, distance from the sea and monsoon winds to the climatic differences each produces - the controls that set out where climatic regions lie. Not LO-28, because no effect on people's lives is asked for.

Reads a map to assign a climate type to Leh, Chennai, Delhi, Panaji and Jaipur - literally locating climatic regions. Not LO-28, since the answer table stops at climate and its cause, not at how people live.
A map task: draw the summer and winter monsoon on India and label the wind directions. Filed as map work rather than LO-26, which is used here for items that explain why the winds reverse.
Baisakhi and Onam as festivals tied to farming and the seasons is climate shaping cultural life. Not LO-27, because nothing is located.
Writing as a farmer preparing for the monsoon - ploughing, bunds, seed choice - is the climate-and-livelihood outcome. Not LO-29: a normal monsoon is being prepared for, not a disaster.

Asks for causes, impacts and what individuals, communities and government can do to reduce a disaster's impact - preventive action stated outright. Not LO-31, because the subject is a hazard rather than resource conservation.
The six ritus are the Indian cultural reckoning of the seasons, with festivals attached. Not LO-27, because the ritus divide the year, not the map.

Revolution and axial tilt determining how much direct sunlight a place gets is the basis on which climatic zones are set out. Not LO-26, because the answer is about the earth-sun geometry, not the make-up of the atmosphere.
Characterises the alpine climate of the Himalayas - one of the climate types this chapter maps. Not LO-28, because no life in that climate is described.
Places the subtropical climate in the northern plains, against three other regions. A locate-the-climatic-region item; the wheat reference is only a clue, so LO-28 would overstate it.
Contrasts arid Thar with the tropical wet west coast on rainfall - two climatic regions compared. Not LO-26, because rainfall totals rather than atmospheric mechanism decide the key.
The angle of the sun's rays making low latitudes warmer is the reason climatic zones run in belts. Not LO-26, since the answer is about incoming solar energy, not about the air itself.

Temperature falling steadily with height, explained through thinner air and distance from the radiating surface, is the vertical structure of the atmosphere. Not LO-27, because no place or region is involved.

Two named places at the same latitude differ because of altitude - a comparison of local climates. Not LO-26: the general lapse of temperature with height has its own item, whereas this one resolves Ooty against Coimbatore.
The sea's moderating effect explaining the coastal-inland contrast is one of the controls that distinguishes climatic regions. Not LO-28, because no human consequence is drawn.

Hot desert winds from Arabia producing summer heat waves in Punjab and Haryana is a regional climate characteristic. Not LO-29, because the item names the phenomenon and never reaches warnings or precautions.

The stem asks for 'topography' specifically as a factor determining climate, so it belongs with the climate controls. Not C-SST1.1, which would be right if the item were about the landforms themselves rather than their climatic role.

The Himalayas shielding India from cold Central Asian winds is a control that makes the northern climate what it is. Not LO-26, because the barrier is a landform effect on regional climate rather than atmospheric structure.
Defines 'microclimate' as a climate confined to a small area - the vocabulary of climatic distribution. Not LO-28, since no inhabitants are mentioned.

'Mausim' meaning season is glossed in the answer as the seasonal reversal of winds, which is the atmospheric circulation behind the monsoon. Not LO-28, because the item is about the word and the wind, not about Indian seasonal life.
Ocean-to-land flow from high to low pressure carrying moisture is the mechanism of the summer monsoon. Not LO-27, because no region is located - the pressure system is the answer.
Contrasts the wet southwest and dry northeast monsoon by the direction of flow - again circulation. Not LO-27, since the item is about the two wind regimes rather than where each brings rain.

Mawsynram as the wettest place, attributed to its position and the monsoon, is a fact about the distribution of rainfall. Not LO-26, because the item asks which place holds the record, not how the rain forms.
Matches Sharad to autumn among the traditional ritus - the Indian seasonal calendar. Filed with the other ritu items under climate-and-life rather than under the map outcome.

Defines a cyclone as an intense low-pressure system with spiralling winds - a structure within the atmosphere. Not LO-29, because nothing about warning or protection is asked; the definitional cyclone items are kept apart from the preparedness ones.
The calm eye inside the eyewall is the internal structure of a storm system. Same reasoning as the cyclone definition: LO-29 is reserved for the items about response.
The IMD's role in tracking cyclones and issuing warnings is the early-warning half of disaster preparedness. Not LO-26, because the storm's physics is not what the item tests.
A glacial lake outburst flood is defined by the catastrophic downstream flooding it causes, which puts it in the flood-disaster lane. Not LO-25, since no landform is being built.

Impermeable concrete raising runoff and overwhelming drains is the cause of urban flooding, the analysis that any preventive measure has to start from. Not LO-30, because the problem is water, not pollution.
The NDRF's remit across natural and human-made disasters is disaster response machinery. Not LO-27, because no climatic region is involved.

Defines climate change as long-term shifts driven since the 1800s mainly by burning fossil fuels, so the causal content is human emissions into the air. Not LO-27, which covers where climates sit, not how they are being altered.

Fossil-fuel burning releasing greenhouse gases that trap heat is an analysis of what is degrading the air. Not LO-31, which would apply to an item urging conservation rather than diagnosing the cause.
'Resilience' is defined as the capacity to withstand and recover from climate-related disasters, which is the disaster-preparedness vocabulary. Not LO-30, because no pollutant is involved.
Sea walls and raised homes against rising seas and stronger storms are concrete preventive measures. Not LO-31, since the community is protecting itself rather than conserving a resource.
Finds the false pairing among India's climate types, keyed on the tropical wet west coast. A climatic-region classification item, not LO-26 atmospheric mechanism.
Mumbai against Nagpur, with the sea's slower heating as the stated reason, is the maritime-continental contrast between two places. Not LO-28, because no aspect of the two cities' life is at issue.

The keyed statements concern where the two monsoons bring rain and how the Western Ghats redistribute it - rainfall distribution across regions. Not LO-26, because the wind mechanism is assumed and the geography of the rain is the point.

Defines fossil fuels, which this chapter introduces as the source of the greenhouse gases altering the atmosphere. Not CG-SST1: the goal's resource clause would fit a mining item, whereas here the fuel matters as a cause of emissions.
Identifies Hemanta as the pre-winter ritu, part of the Indian seasonal reckoning. Same lane as the other ritu items.

An urban heat island is a local climate warmer than its surroundings because of surfaces and missing vegetation - a microclimate, matching the microclimate item. Not LO-30, because the answer turns on heat absorption and green cover rather than on pollutants.
